question.text: How much distance does a safe, complete stop take?

answer.text: Bringing a vehicle to a safe, complete stop takes a long distance.

teaching.text: Bringing your vehicle to a safe, complete stop takes a long distance. Remember: stopping takes distance.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Bringing a vehicle to a safe, complete stop takes a long distance.

question.text: What does braking distance depend on?

answer.text: Braking distance depends on your speed, your perception and reaction times, the pavement, your tires, your vehicle's weight including any load or trailer, and the type and condition of your brakes.

teaching.text: Speed, perception and reaction times, pavement, tires, vehicle weight with any load, and brakes all change braking distance. Remember: speed, reaction, road, tires, weight, brakes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Braking distance depends on your speed, your perception and reaction times, the pavement, your tires, your vehicle's weight including any load or trailer, and the type and condition of your brakes.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: speed, reaction, road, tires, weight, brakes

question.text: What is perception time, and how long does it average?

answer.text: Perception time, the time it takes a driver to see and recognize a dangerous situation, averages zero point seven five seconds.

teaching.text: Perception time is how long it takes to see and recognize a danger, and it averages zero point seven five seconds. Remember: see it: zero point seven five.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Perception time, the time it takes a driver to see and recognize a dangerous situation, averages zero point seven five seconds.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: see it: zero point seven five

question.text: What is reaction time, and how long does it average?

answer.text: Reaction time, the gap between perceiving danger and starting to brake, averages zero point seven five seconds.

teaching.text: Reaction time runs from perceiving danger to starting to brake, and it averages zero point seven five seconds. Remember: start braking: zero point seven five.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Reaction time, the gap between perceiving danger and starting to brake, averages zero point seven five seconds.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: start braking: zero point seven five

question.text: On average, how long does a person need to perceive a threat and react?

answer.text: On average a person needs one point five seconds to perceive a threat in the roadway and react to it.

teaching.text: An average person needs one point five seconds to perceive a threat in the roadway and react to it. Remember: one point five seconds.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On average a person needs one point five seconds to perceive a threat in the roadway and react to it.

question.text: How do perception time and reaction time add up?

answer.text: Perception time and reaction time each average zero point seven five seconds, and together they make the one point five seconds an average driver needs before braking begins.

teaching.text: Perception time and reaction time each average zero point seven five seconds, adding up to one point five seconds before braking begins. Remember: point seven five twice.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Perception time and reaction time each average zero point seven five seconds, and together they make the one point five seconds an average driver needs before braking begins.

question.text: How does knowing your stopping distance help you?

answer.text: Knowing how far your vehicle needs to stop helps you pick a safe driving speed.

teaching.text: When you know how far your vehicle needs to stop, you can pick a safe driving speed. Remember: pick a safe speed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Knowing how far your vehicle needs to stop helps you pick a safe driving speed.

question.text: Why is the stopping-distance chart only a guide?

answer.text: The manual's stopping-distance chart is only a guide, because your real stopping distance depends on factors such as your tires, brakes and the road.

teaching.text: The stopping-distance chart is only a guide, since your tires, brakes and the road change your true stopping distance. Remember: your car and road differ.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The manual's stopping-distance chart is only a guide, because your real stopping distance depends on factors such as your tires, brakes and the road.

question.text: What following distance should you keep in most situations?

answer.text: Keep a following distance of at least three seconds in most driving situations, so you can avoid a crash if traffic ahead stops suddenly.

teaching.text: In most driving, stay at least three seconds behind so you can avoid a crash if traffic ahead stops suddenly. Remember: three seconds minimum.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Keep a following distance of at least three seconds in most driving situations, so you can avoid a crash if traffic ahead stops suddenly.

question.text: What following distance do some situations call for?

answer.text: Some situations call for a longer following distance of three to six seconds.

teaching.text: Some driving situations call for a longer following distance of three to six seconds. Remember: three to six seconds.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Some situations call for a longer following distance of three to six seconds.

question.text: What following distance do slippery roads call for?

answer.text: On slippery roads, double your following distance to six seconds or more so you have room to adjust your speed or stop.

teaching.text: On slippery roads, double your following distance to six seconds or more for room to slow or stop. Remember: double to six or more.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On slippery roads, double your following distance to six seconds or more so you have room to adjust your speed or stop.

question.text: How do the everyday and slippery-road following distances compare?

answer.text: The everyday minimum is a three-second following distance, while slippery roads call for doubling it to six seconds or more.

teaching.text: The everyday minimum following distance is three seconds, and slippery roads call for doubling it to six seconds or more. Remember: three, then double to six.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The everyday minimum is a three-second following distance, while slippery roads call for doubling it to six seconds or more.

question.text: The driver behind you wants to pass. What helps?

answer.text: If the driver behind you wants to pass, slowing down lets that driver get by sooner and gives more room to pull back into the lane.

teaching.text: Slowing down lets a driver who wants to pass get by sooner, with more room to pull back into the lane. Remember: slow down, let them by.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If the driver behind you wants to pass, slowing down lets that driver get by sooner and gives more room to pull back into the lane.

question.text: When someone behind wants to pass, should you slow down or speed up?

answer.text: When someone behind you wants to pass, the right move is to slow down, not to speed up.

teaching.text: When someone behind you wants to pass, slow down; do not speed up. Remember: slow, never speed up.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When someone behind you wants to pass, the right move is to slow down, not to speed up.

question.text: A tractor-trailer blocks your view ahead. What should you do?

answer.text: When a large vehicle such as a tractor-trailer blocks your view ahead, drop back farther so you can see around it.

teaching.text: When a tractor-trailer or other large vehicle blocks your view, drop back farther so you can see around it. Remember: drop back to see.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a large vehicle such as a tractor-trailer blocks your view ahead, drop back farther so you can see around it.

question.text: Is a quiet, empty rural highway safe by default?

answer.text: A quiet, empty rural highway can carry as much danger as busy city traffic.

teaching.text: A quiet, empty rural highway can carry as much danger as busy city traffic does. Remember: quiet roads carry danger too.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A quiet, empty rural highway can carry as much danger as busy city traffic.

question.text: What are common rural road hazards?

answer.text: Common rural hazards include animals on the road, slow farm equipment just past the top of a hill, and low spots covered with water.

teaching.text: Rural hazards include animals on the road, slow farm equipment just past a hilltop, and low spots covered with water. Remember: animals, farm gear, water.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Common rural hazards include animals on the road, slow farm equipment just past the top of a hill, and low spots covered with water.

question.text: How should you drive on open rural roads?

answer.text: On open rural roads, stay alert, watch for warning signs and slow down as you near curves or hills that hide the road ahead.

teaching.text: On open rural roads, stay alert, watch for warning signs, and slow down near curves or hills that hide the road. Remember: slow for curves and hills.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On open rural roads, stay alert, watch for warning signs and slow down as you near curves or hills that hide the road ahead.

question.text: In bad weather, what two problems often happen together?

answer.text: In bad weather, poor visibility and poor traction often happen at the same time.

teaching.text: In bad weather, poor visibility and poor traction often arrive together. Remember: poor visibility, poor traction.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In bad weather, poor visibility and poor traction often happen at the same time.

question.text: How do changing road and weather conditions affect you?

answer.text: Changing road and weather conditions shorten the time you have to react and affect how your car handles.

teaching.text: Changing road and weather conditions shorten your time to react and change how your car handles. Remember: less time to react.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Changing road and weather conditions shorten the time you have to react and affect how your car handles.

question.text: What is the first rule in bad conditions?

answer.text: In bad conditions the first rule is to reduce speed, which offsets the visibility and reaction time you have lost.

teaching.text: The first rule in bad conditions is to reduce speed, which offsets the visibility and reaction time you have lost. Remember: reduce speed first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In bad conditions the first rule is to reduce speed, which offsets the visibility and reaction time you have lost.

question.text: When does driving toward the sun create glare?

answer.text: Driving toward the sun in the early morning or late afternoon creates glare.

teaching.text: Driving toward the sun in the early morning or late afternoon creates glare. Remember: early morning, late afternoon.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Driving toward the sun in the early morning or late afternoon creates glare.

question.text: What helps cut down sun glare?

answer.text: Sunglasses, clean windows and sun visors all help cut down sun glare.

teaching.text: Sunglasses, clean windows and sun visors all help cut down sun glare. Remember: sunglasses, clean glass, visors.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Sunglasses, clean windows and sun visors all help cut down sun glare.

question.text: With the sun behind you, who may not see your car?

answer.text: When the sun is behind you, oncoming drivers may be facing the glare and may not see your car or your signals.

teaching.text: With the sun behind you, oncoming drivers may face the glare and may not see your car or your signals. Remember: oncoming drivers face glare.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When the sun is behind you, oncoming drivers may be facing the glare and may not see your car or your signals.

question.text: How does sun glare differ when the sun is ahead of you versus behind you?

answer.text: With the sun ahead of you, you face the glare, but with the sun behind you, oncoming drivers face it and may not see you.

teaching.text: With the sun ahead you face the glare, and with the sun behind you oncoming drivers face it and may not see you. Remember: ahead: you; behind: them.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: With the sun ahead of you, you face the glare, but with the sun behind you, oncoming drivers face it and may not see you.

question.text: What kind of wind makes a vehicle harder to control?

answer.text: Strong winds, and crosswinds in particular, make a vehicle harder to control.

teaching.text: Strong winds, and crosswinds in particular, make a vehicle harder to control. Remember: crosswinds especially.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Strong winds, and crosswinds in particular, make a vehicle harder to control.

question.text: Which vehicles are most at risk in wind?

answer.text: Wind is very dangerous for campers, large recreational vehicles and anyone towing a trailer, and it also makes lightweight vehicles harder to control.

teaching.text: Wind is very dangerous for campers, large recreational vehicles and anyone towing a trailer, and it also affects lightweight vehicles. Remember: campers, RVs, trailers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Wind is very dangerous for campers, large recreational vehicles and anyone towing a trailer, and it also makes lightweight vehicles harder to control.

question.text: How can you gain more control in a strong wind?

answer.text: To gain more control in a strong wind, slow down.

teaching.text: Slowing down gives you more control when a strong wind is blowing. Remember: slow down.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To gain more control in a strong wind, slow down.

question.text: When should you expect crosswinds?

answer.text: When you leave a sheltered stretch for open space, expect crosswinds that may push you toward the side or the middle of the road.

teaching.text: Leaving a sheltered stretch for open space, expect crosswinds that may push you toward the side or middle of the road. Remember: leaving shelter for open space.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When you leave a sheltered stretch for open space, expect crosswinds that may push you toward the side or the middle of the road.

question.text: Where are crosswinds most likely, and where can they push you?

answer.text: Crosswinds are most likely when you come out of a sheltered stretch into open space, and they can push you toward the edge or the middle of the road.

teaching.text: Crosswinds are most likely when you leave a sheltered stretch for open space, and they can push you toward the edge or middle. Remember: open space pushes sideways.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Crosswinds are most likely when you come out of a sheltered stretch into open space, and they can push you toward the edge or the middle of the road.

question.text: What may wind do to a vehicle pulling a trailer?

answer.text: Wind may make a vehicle that is pulling a trailer sway.

teaching.text: Wind may make a vehicle that is pulling a trailer start to sway. Remember: trailer may sway.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Wind may make a vehicle that is pulling a trailer sway.

question.text: What may gusts from large trucks or buses force you to do?

answer.text: Gusts created by large trucks or buses you meet may force you to make steering corrections.

teaching.text: Gusts from large trucks or buses you meet may force you to make steering corrections. Remember: steering corrections.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Gusts created by large trucks or buses you meet may force you to make steering corrections.

question.text: What can wind currents cause a towing vehicle to do?

answer.text: Wind currents can cause a vehicle pulling a trailer to jackknife.

teaching.text: Wind currents can cause a vehicle that is pulling a trailer to jackknife. Remember: jackknife risk.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Wind currents can cause a vehicle pulling a trailer to jackknife.

question.text: You are towing a trailer and a truck passes on your left. What do you do?

answer.text: If you are towing a trailer and a truck or bus passes on your left, move as far right in your lane as you can and slow down, then speed up gently as it goes by so the trailer tracks straight.

teaching.text: Towing as a truck or bus passes on your left, move far right in your lane and slow, then speed up gently as it goes by. Remember: move right, slow, speed gently.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you are towing a trailer and a truck or bus passes on your left, move as far right in your lane as you can and slow down, then speed up gently as it goes by so the trailer tracks straight.

question.text: When towing as a truck passes on the left, what is the order of moves?

answer.text: When towing a trailer as a truck or bus passes on the left, you first move right and slow down, and then speed up only gently as it passes.

teaching.text: When towing as a truck or bus passes on the left, first move right and slow down, then speed up only gently. Remember: right and slow, then gentle.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When towing a trailer as a truck or bus passes on the left, you first move right and slow down, and then speed up only gently as it passes.

question.text: How does a strong headwind affect driving?

answer.text: Driving into a strong headwind may take more acceleration and makes steering harder.

teaching.text: A strong headwind may take more acceleration and makes steering harder. Remember: more gas, harder steering.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Driving into a strong headwind may take more acceleration and makes steering harder.

question.text: How should you handle a tailwind?

answer.text: A tailwind pushes your speed up, so you must slow down and start braking earlier to stop.

teaching.text: A tailwind pushes your speed up, so slow down and start braking earlier to stop. Remember: slow and brake earlier.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A tailwind pushes your speed up, so you must slow down and start braking earlier to stop.

question.text: How do a headwind and a tailwind call for different driving?

answer.text: A headwind calls for more acceleration and firmer steering, while a tailwind calls for slowing and braking earlier.

teaching.text: A headwind calls for more acceleration and firmer steering, while a tailwind calls for slowing and braking earlier. Remember: headwind push, tailwind brake early.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A headwind calls for more acceleration and firmer steering, while a tailwind calls for slowing and braking earlier.

question.text: How badly can an Arizona dust storm cut visibility?

answer.text: Dust storms are common in Arizona and can sometimes cut a driver's visibility to zero.

teaching.text: Dust storms are common in Arizona and can sometimes cut a driver's visibility all the way to zero. Remember: down to zero.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Dust storms are common in Arizona and can sometimes cut a driver's visibility to zero.

question.text: What should you do first when you run into a dust storm?

answer.text: If you run into a dust storm, check the traffic around you at once and begin slowing down.

teaching.text: When you run into a dust storm, check the traffic around you at once and begin slowing down. Remember: check traffic, start slowing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you run into a dust storm, check the traffic around you at once and begin slowing down.

question.text: When should you pull off the road in a dust storm?

answer.text: Pull off the road as soon as you can in a dust storm, rather than waiting until poor visibility makes it hard to do safely.

teaching.text: In a dust storm, pull off the road as soon as you can rather than waiting until it becomes hard to do safely. Remember: as soon as you can.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Pull off the road as soon as you can in a dust storm, rather than waiting until poor visibility makes it hard to do safely.

question.text: Should you wait until you cannot see before pulling off in a dust storm?

answer.text: Pull off early in a dust storm, before visibility drops, rather than waiting until you can no longer see to leave the road safely.

teaching.text: Pull off early in a dust storm, before visibility drops, instead of waiting until you can no longer see. Remember: pull off early.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Pull off early in a dust storm, before visibility drops, rather than waiting until you can no longer see to leave the road safely.

question.text: In a severe dust storm, where should you stop?

answer.text: In a severe dust storm, slow down immediately, drive all the way off the highway and stop as far to the right as you can.

teaching.text: In a severe dust storm, slow down at once, drive all the way off the highway and stop as far right as you can. Remember: fully off, far right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a severe dust storm, slow down immediately, drive all the way off the highway and stop as far to the right as you can.

question.text: During a dust storm, where must you never stop?

answer.text: During a dust storm, never stop in a travel lane or in the emergency lane.

teaching.text: During a dust storm, never stop in a travel lane and never stop in the emergency lane. Remember: no travel or emergency lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: During a dust storm, never stop in a travel lane or in the emergency lane.

question.text: After pulling off in a severe dust storm, what do you do with your lights and brake?

answer.text: After pulling off in a severe dust storm, turn your lights off and take your foot off the brake.

teaching.text: After pulling off in a severe dust storm, turn your lights off and take your foot off the brake. Remember: lights off, foot off.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After pulling off in a severe dust storm, turn your lights off and take your foot off the brake.

question.text: In a severe dust storm, where do you stop and what do you switch off?

answer.text: In a severe dust storm you leave the highway completely, avoiding both the travel lane and the emergency lane, and then switch off your lights and release the brake.

teaching.text: In a severe dust storm, leave the highway completely, stay out of travel and emergency lanes, then lights off and brake released. Remember: fully off, lights off.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a severe dust storm you leave the highway completely, avoiding both the travel lane and the emergency lane, and then switch off your lights and release the brake.

question.text: Where should you stay until a dust storm passes?

answer.text: Stay inside the vehicle with seat belts buckled until the dust storm has passed.

teaching.text: Stay inside your vehicle with seat belts buckled until the dust storm has passed. Remember: inside, buckled up.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Stay inside the vehicle with seat belts buckled until the dust storm has passed.

question.text: When is heavy rain especially hazardous?

answer.text: Heavy rain is especially hazardous when it comes with gusty winds, as in a thunderstorm.

teaching.text: Heavy rain is especially hazardous when it comes with gusty winds, as in a thunderstorm. Remember: rain plus gusty wind.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Heavy rain is especially hazardous when it comes with gusty winds, as in a thunderstorm.

question.text: In heavy rain, which vehicles are especially hard to see?

answer.text: In heavy rain, vehicles behind you and in your blind spots are especially hard to see.

teaching.text: In heavy rain, vehicles behind you and in your blind spots are especially hard to see. Remember: behind you and blind spots.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In heavy rain, vehicles behind you and in your blind spots are especially hard to see.

question.text: Why wait a short time before switching on your wipers?

answer.text: Wait a short time after rain begins before switching on your wipers, because blades on a dirty windshield can smear it.

teaching.text: Wait a short time after rain begins before using wipers, because blades on a dirty windshield can smear it. Remember: dirty glass smears.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Wait a short time after rain begins before switching on your wipers, because blades on a dirty windshield can smear it.

question.text: How big a following gap should you allow in rain?

answer.text: In rain, slow down so the gap to the vehicle ahead grows to at least six seconds.

teaching.text: In rain, slow down until the gap to the vehicle ahead grows to at least six seconds. Remember: six seconds or more.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In rain, slow down so the gap to the vehicle ahead grows to at least six seconds.

question.text: When is a wet road especially slippery?

answer.text: Take extra care in the first thirty minutes of rain, when road grime and oil mix with water and make the surface slippery.

teaching.text: The first thirty minutes of rain need extra care, as road grime and oil mix with water and make the surface slippery. Remember: first thirty minutes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Take extra care in the first thirty minutes of rain, when road grime and oil mix with water and make the surface slippery.

question.text: What do the six seconds and thirty minutes figures for rain mean?

answer.text: Rain calls for a gap of at least six seconds, while the thirty minutes figure marks the especially slippery period after rain starts.

teaching.text: Rain calls for at least six seconds of following distance, and the first thirty minutes after rain starts are especially slippery. Remember: gap versus slippery window.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Rain calls for a gap of at least six seconds, while the thirty minutes figure marks the especially slippery period after rain starts.

question.text: At what speed can tires lose all road contact in heavy rain?

answer.text: In heavy rain, tires can ride up on a film of water, and at fifty miles per hour they can lose all contact with the road.

teaching.text: In heavy rain, tires can ride up on a film of water and can lose all road contact at fifty miles per hour. Remember: fifty miles per hour.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In heavy rain, tires can ride up on a film of water, and at fifty miles per hour they can lose all contact with the road.

question.text: Which tires lose contact with a wet road at lower speeds?

answer.text: Tires that are under-inflated, worn or bald lose contact with a wet road at much lower speeds.

teaching.text: Under-inflated, worn or bald tires lose contact with a wet road at much lower speeds. Remember: worn, bald, under-inflated.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Tires that are under-inflated, worn or bald lose contact with a wet road at much lower speeds.

question.text: How do good tires and worn tires differ in heavy rain?

answer.text: In heavy rain, tires can lose all road contact at fifty miles per hour, while worn, bald or under-inflated tires can lose it at much lower speeds.

teaching.text: In heavy rain tires can lose all contact at fifty miles per hour, and worn, bald or under-inflated tires at much lower speeds. Remember: fifty versus much lower.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In heavy rain, tires can lose all road contact at fifty miles per hour, while worn, bald or under-inflated tires can lose it at much lower speeds.

question.text: What is the best way to prevent hydroplaning?

answer.text: Slowing down is the best way to prevent hydroplaning.

teaching.text: Slowing down is the best way to prevent hydroplaning on a wet road. Remember: slow down.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Slowing down is the best way to prevent hydroplaning.
